_comment: Keycloak realm for MIR — BUILD_SPEC P4.1, P4.3.
Import with: kcadm.sh create realms -f realm-mir.json, or KC_IMPORT on first boot.
WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT CONTAIN, ON PURPOSE:
* no client secrets — injected from AWS Secrets Manager at deploy time (BUILD_SPEC §6)
* no users — created through the application, never seeded here
SELF-HOSTED (ADR / §4): self-hosting Keycloak keeps identity out of the
compliance chain. A hosted IdP would become a processor of authentication
data for patients in two jurisdictions whose rules (L1, L2) are unresolved.
_comment_identifiers: Login is by phone number, not email. Libyan patients frequently have no
email address, and the phone number is the identifier the claim flow
(P5.2) and SMS OTP both key on.
_comment_tokens: Short access tokens: a stolen token is useful only for its remaining
lifetime, and this system's tokens grant reach toward patient imaging.
Refresh is longer so a doctor mid-upload is not thrown out, but idle
sessions still expire within a working day.
_comment_bruteforce: Server-side brute-force protection, in addition to the application rate
limiter (P4.5). Two layers because they fail differently: Keycloak's
survives an application restart, the application's covers endpoints
passwordPolicy: length(12) and notUsername(undefined) and notEmail(undefined) and passwordHistory(5) and hashAlgorithm(pbkdf2-sha512) and hashIterations(210000)

realm.name: libya_doctor
realm.description: Referring doctor in Libya. Creates patient records, uploads studies. MFA required.

realm.name: tunisia_doctor
realm.description: Receiving doctor in Tunisia. Manages availability, reads consented studies. MFA required.

realm.name: patient
realm.description: Patient or client. Claims their record, grants consent, books appointments.

realm.name: admin
realm.description: Platform admin. Doctor verification and support. NO routine access to patient images (BUILD_SPEC §1.1). MFA required.

the URL, where they reach browser history and referrer headers.
